subject: Hightail order form – SLA credit ladder and maintenance window language
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@hightailhealth.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: tom.alvarez@hightailhealth.com, legal@hightailhealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Order form – SLA credit ladder and maintenance window language

Laura —

Thanks for the redline. We're close but Procurement and Legal have flagged two items they need clarified before we can route to execs: the service credit ladder for partial-month outages and the permitted scheduled maintenance window and notification timing. Attached is our Order Form with inline comments (Hightail_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf).

Key asks from our side:
- Can Redwood clarify the outage credit calculation when the monthly uptime percentage falls between tiers? Our lawyers prefer a pro-rated / tiered ladder rather than a single bucket.
- We need explicit language describing planned maintenance windows (max duration / frequency) and the notification timeline (we asked for 7 days).
- For P1 incident response time: Hightail requests 30-minute initial acknowledgement and a 2-hour follow-up plan.

Can you share a proposal we can take to our legal counsel? If you can provide a tracked version of the SLA clause and a clean order form with proposed credit calculations we can expedite.

Thanks — Samantha
Samantha Lee
Sr. Procurement Manager | Hightail Health
Samantha.Lee@hightailhealth.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@hightailhealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form – SLA credit ladder and maintenance window language

Samantha —

Appreciate the clear list. We've reviewed your PDF and attached a proposed tracked change (Redwood-SLA-proposal-tracked.docx) and a companion spreadsheet that models the credit ladder (SLA-credit-ladder.xlsx). Summary of our proposal below so you have it up front:

1) Uptime SLO and credit ladder (monthly uptime percentage measured end-of-month):
   - 99.95% and above: no credit
   - 99.90% to <99.95%: 5% of monthly fee credit
   - 99.00% to <99.90%: 20% of monthly fee credit
   - <99.00%: 50% of monthly fee credit (capped at 100% for the month)
   - We propose the credit be applied pro rata for partial-month billing cycles; spreadsheet models both bucketed and pro-rated calculations.

2) Scheduled maintenance (planned maintenance):
   - Standard: up to 4 hours per month as part of regular maintenance (no credit).
   - Major maintenance: up to 8 hours per month but requires advanced agreement.
   - Notification: 72 hours for standard, 7 days for major maintenance. We can accept 7 days for any maintenance that will exceed 4 hours.

3) Incident response commitments (initial reply / mitigation plan):
   - P1 (system unavailable): initial acknowledgement within 30 minutes, targeted mitigation plan within 2 hours, continuous updates every 60 minutes until resolution.
   - P2 (degraded service): acknowledgement within 2 hours, remediation target within 8 business hours.

4) Emergency maintenance: allowed with 4 hours notice and reasonable effort to minimize impact; emergency events that cause downtime will still count toward uptime calculations and credit ladders.

5) Exclusions: force majeure, customer misconfigurations, third-party provider outages (we list the common ones).

Next steps proposed: Marcus (legal/ops) and Grace (technical ops) will take your redlines and update final clause text; Neha can step in for commercial if any pricing impacts are needed. If Hightail accepts the ladder above, we can prepare a clean order form for signature by end of week.

I attached the tracked doc and the spreadsheet. Let me know a time for a 30-min call if you'd prefer to walk through the ladder.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 650-555-0147

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@hightailhealth.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@hightailhealth.com>, legal@hightailhealth.com
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form – SLA credit ladder and maintenance window language

Laura / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple quick reactions from Product and Legal: the ladder helps but Legal wants the calculation method spelled out (i.e., measurement period, rounding, and whether credits are the exclusive remedy). Also Product is pushing back on the 4-hour monthly allowance and asks whether we can limit to two maintenance windows per month rather than a fixed hour cap.

We can probably accept 72-hour notice for standard work but insist on 7 days for anything that impacts availability for more than 2 hours. Can you add explicit language for how credit is triggered (e.g., measured at region level, remediation time accounted into downtime)?

We should sync on a short call tomorrow. I can do 11:00am PT.

—Tom
Tom Alvarez
VP Product | Hightail Health

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@hightailhealth.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@hightailhealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form – SLA credit ladder and maintenance window language

Tom / Samantha —

Thanks — confirmed 11:00am PT works. A few clarifications I will bring to the call from legal/ops so we can resolve on the spot:

- Measurement: Monthly uptime percentage will be calculated per-customer, per-region, measured over UTC calendar month. We round to two decimal places; the spreadsheet shows examples.
- Credits as exclusive remedy: Redwood requests credits be the exclusive financial remedy for SLA noncompliance; we are open to adding carve-outs for willful misconduct but would prefer caps instead of open-ended indemnities.
- Maintenance language: We can model maintenance as up to two scheduled windows/month (each up to 3 hours) without credit, and an allowance to consolidate into a single 6-hour window if mutually agreed in writing. Major maintenance (>3 hours) requires 7 days notice. We’ll include a clause that maintenance outside scheduled windows will be used sparingly and treated as emergency maintenance.

I'll bring a redline highlighting the exclusive-remedy language and the exact maintenance paragraph. If we can agree on the two-window approach and the credit ladder phrasing, we should be able to finalize the Order Form and prepare a DocuSign packet.

Marcus Lin
Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0122

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@hightailhealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@hightailhealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form – SLA credit ladder and maintenance window language

All —

Good sync this morning. To capture next steps and decisions from the call:

- Agreed items:
  • Credit ladder: use the tiered ladder we proposed (99.95/99.90/99.00/<99.00) with pro-rated calculation option if Hightail prefers — Hightail to confirm preference in writing.
  • Measurement: per-customer, per-region, UTC month, round to two decimals.
  • Maintenance: Redwood to adopt two scheduled windows/month (each up to 3 hours) as default; capacity to consolidate to a single 6-hour window by mutual written agreement. Major maintenance (>3 hours) requires 7 days notice.
  • P1 response: 30-min ack, 2-hour mitigation plan target.

- Outstanding items:
  • Hightail to confirm whether they want pro-rated credit calculation vs bucketed.
  • Legal (Hightail) to confirm acceptance of credits as exclusive financial remedy; Redwood is open to carving out gross negligence / willful misconduct.

Next actions:
- Laura/Marcus: we'll push the agreed redline into a final tracked doc and prepare a clean Order Form for DocuSign.
- Samantha/Tom: confirm pro-rate vs bucketed choice and any final language edits.

I'll attach the updated tracked doc after we finalize the pro-rate question; aiming for a signature-ready packet by Friday.

Thanks,
Laura

Attachment references: Redwood-SLA-proposal-tracked.docx (contains proposed clause text and exclusive-remedy language). Spreadsheet models: SLA-credit-ladder.xlsx.
